title: Module 8 · Lesson 2 — Drift, regression and the maintenance loop

lines: Welcome to Module Eight, Lesson Two: drift, regression, and the maintenance loop.
Agents degrade even when nobody touches them.
Picture CampusDesk, a university helpdesk agent that answers student questions.
All summer, nobody changes a line of its code.

say.0: Picture Campus Desk, a university help desk agent that answers student questions.

lines: By September, its answers are noticeably worse.
The world around it changed, and that's drift.
Input drift: students ask new things, in new ways.
Spot it by tracking query topics and embeddings over time.
Corpus drift: the wiki was reorganised, so retrieval quality moved.
Re-run retrieval evaluation on a fixed set of queries to catch it.
Model drift: the provider silently updated its hosted model.
Pin versions to prevent it, and run a golden set continuously to detect it.
Tool drift: the enrollment system's API changed its schema.
Scheduled contract tests against every tool catch that.

say.0: Tool drift: the enrollment system's A P I changed its schema.

lines: So run the golden set against production on a schedule, not only in CI.
That catches drift that no code change caused.

say.0: So run the golden set against production on a schedule, not only in C I.

lines: Sample live traffic for automated scoring, and send uncertain cases to a small human queue.
Track every metric against a baseline.
When an incident hits, first contain it with a previous version or a safe fallback.
A degraded answer beats a confidently wrong one.
Next, diagnose from traces: pull the failing runs and find the common span.
Then fix the right layer, whether prompt, schema, tool, retrieval, or model version.
Add the failing case to the golden set, or you'll ship it again.
Then ask what guard would have caught it sooner.
Version prompts, tool schemas, retrieval settings, models, and guardrails together.
Record that version on every trace, so any output can be reproduced.
Gate changes on the golden set, then roll out through shadow and canary, with a tested rollback.
Even a one-word prompt edit is a production change.
On the exam, an agent that degrades with no deployment means something upstream changed.
The fix is pinned versions, a golden set, and contract tests, so read on for the full loop.
